1.name: Trim wheel
1.spec: Ø230, finger grips, in the pedestal
1.note: Roll the top aft for nose up. 6.4 turns cover the tab from stop to stop; 2.2 turns trim the change from 110 to 65 kt. Fine enough to set the stick force to nothing.

2.name: Cockpit drum
2.note: Turns with the wheel and winds the cable loop: one strand off its top, the other off its bottom. 188 mm of cable a turn.

3.name: Position indicator
3.spec: Pointer in a slot, geared to the shaft
3.note: Shows where the tab is set, from DN to UP, with a take-off mark. Before take-off the pilot sets it there: trimmed for the climb-out speed.

4.name: Pedestal
4.spec: Two side plates and a cover
4.note: Between the front seats. Carries the wheel's shaft and the indicator; the wheel's rim stands through a slot in its cover.

5.name: Trim cables
5.note: From the cockpit drum under the floor and up the tail cone to the actuator's drum. One strand pulls while the other pays out; a turnbuckle keeps the loop tight.

6.name: Pulleys
6.note: A pair under the cabin floor and a pair at the tail turn the loop toward the elevator's hinge line, so the elevator's movement neither pulls nor slackens the cables.

7.name: Actuator drum
7.note: Pinned to the screw. The cable arrives along the hinge line and wraps two and a half turns; both strands walk along the groove as it turns.

8.name: Jackscrew
8.note: 2 mm of nut travel a turn. Its lead angle is 4.0°, under the 8.5° friction angle of bronze on steel: the nut cannot turn it, so the air load can never wind the tab back.

9.name: Nut
9.note: Runs along the screw as it turns; its lug in the housing's slot stops it turning with the screw and carries the rod's pin. Forward is nose-up trim.

10.name: Ball bearing
10.note: Carries the screw at the drum end and takes the rod's load along the axis either way, so the screw turns freely under load.

11.name: Actuator housing
11.spec: Tube Ø24, slotted below, bearing boss
11.note: Bolted to a rib in the elevator. Its bottom slot guides the nut's lug; stop blocks close the slot's ends.

12.name: Aft bush
12.note: Supports the screw's aft journal: radial load only, the bearing takes the thrust.

13.name: Stop blocks
13.note: The nut's lug lands on them at 10° tab up and 25° down. They, not the cable or the pilot, set the tab's travel.

14.name: Push-pull rod
14.spec: Ø4.8, rod end each side, pins safetied
14.note: From the nut's lug, out through a slot in the lower skin, to the tab's horn. The only thing that holds the tab: if it comes off, the tab is free and flutters.

15.name: Tab horn
15.note: Riveted under the tab. 32 mm of arm: the nut's 2 mm a turn of the screw becomes 3.6° of tab.

16.name: Piano hinge
16.note: Hinges the tab along its whole span to the elevator's rear spar: no point loads, no play to start flutter.

17.name: Trim tab
17.note: 3.1 % of the elevator's area, at the end of its chord. Set down, the air pushes it up, and that moment holds the elevator up: trimmed, the pull is zero.

18.name: Elevator
18.spec: Port half at BL −485, two spars
18.note: Floats to wherever its hinge moment is zero. The tab moves that place to where the flight needs the elevator, so the pilot need hold nothing.
